verdict_text:
NO

The alternation in `matrix_re` omits `self_attn.o_proj.weight`, so only 6 of the 7 listed projection matrices per layer are cast — 96 tensors instead of 112 — and all 16 `model.layers.<i>.self_attn.o_proj.weight` tensors are left in float32, violating Required result clause 1 (and clause 2, since o_proj is not "every other tensor"). The guard `assert sum(...) == 96` encodes the same off-by-one and therefore does not fail loudly, violating the first Required check ("exactly 112 tensors are bfloat16"). Since grading compares dtypes against a hidden reference, the 16 o_proj tensors will mismatch. The remaining behaviour is fine: `buffer_re` with the never-matching `(?!)` deletes nothing (correct per clause 3, though it is dead code), names are unchanged, and the 114-tensor count and sharded output with index are as required.
expected_defect: One projection family is missing from the bfloat16 cast pattern (the attention output projection stays float32); the artifact's own count check was adjusted to the wrong number.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
